sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Skye is a Scottish mythological site. The Isle of Skye lies off the west coast of Scotland. It is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides. The isle was named after the warrior woman Scáthach. She ran a school of battle on the isle. The hero Cúchulainn was sent to train with her so he could become the greatest of the Irish warriors. The isle holds the memory of that school of blades. The shore holds another story. The folk of Skye say the fair-headed families come from the mermaids. The houses named Morrow, MacMorrow, MacCodrum, and MacMurray are their living kin. So the isle joins the battle-school of Scáthach with the sea people who rose from the deep. The name Skye is bound to the woman who gave it the strength of the water and the blade together.
